claims.text: Adding up to 5 wt% Nb to CoCrFeMnNi coatings promotes formation of a wear-induced nanocrystalline mechanically mixed layer.
The wear-induced mechanically mixed layer contains Nb-rich nanoscale precipitates.
The mechanically mixed layer acts as a protective barrier during sliding wear.
Wear-induced nanostructuring reduces wear by impeding dislocation motion and crack initiation.
The proposed wear-reduction effect is distinct from general bulk hardening caused by Nb addition.
The mechanically mixed layer evolves through dynamic recrystallization and strain-induced nanoprecipitation.
Local contact stress, frictional heating, shear, and strain during sliding induce dynamic recrystallization and phase separation.
Nb catalyzes and stabilizes nanoscale precipitate formation in the evolving mechanically mixed layer.
Nb-rich precipitates obstruct dislocation motion and plastic deformation.
Reduced plastic deformation lowers crack initiation and material removal during wear.
Nb-enriched coatings will develop a thicker and more continuous nanocrystalline mechanically mixed layer than the Nb-free baseline.
Nb-enriched coatings will have a higher volume fraction of Nb-rich precipitates than the Nb-free baseline.
Greater development of the precipitate-containing mechanically mixed layer will correlate with a lower wear rate.
Pre-aging Nb-modified coatings can suppress dynamic nanoprecipitation and thereby distinguish the proposed surface-layer mechanism from bulk-hardness effects.
Nb-free CoCrFeMnNi coatings do not form the same robust wear-induced nanocrystalline mechanically mixed layer.
Nb-free CoCrFeMnNi coatings exhibit higher wear rates than Nb-enriched coatings under otherwise identical conditions.
The proposed mechanism should hold for Nb additions up to 5 wt% during dry room-temperature sliding at fixed load and speed.
The proposed mechanism may not hold under substantially different temperatures, loads, or environments.
